::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** Sept 6 1866  
**Manuscript:** Copy outletter book British Library Add MSS.55386 (1) P.387
:::

Dear Miss Yonge,                                                                   Sept 6 1866

We shall look forward to the [Chaplet of Pearls](cmy_books/cmybook_69.qmd) beginning as soon as either[“Old Sir Douglas](other_books/otherbook_469.qmd)” or [“The Silcotes”](other_books/otherbook_1129.qmd)[^1] cease. It will be, I venture to think, one of your most popular books, and ought not to be the worse for a little mellowing.

I am going down to Scotland with[my wife](people/person_940.qmd) tomorrow morning, and will be away for a fortnight. After that I hope to be at home all the winter. We shall be very glad to see any of the worthies when you have done them.

I quite hope that [Mrs Daniel](people/person_941.qmd) is on the way of recovery. She is with us at present at [illegible]  of [illegible]  during our absence.

I hoped to send you’re a/c for the year with this. [Mr Craik](people/person_379.qmd) will in a few days.

I have several other matters which I want to talk to you about when I come back. I will write you very soon.

Very faithfully yours

 A. Macmillan

&nbsp;

---

[^1]: Chapters of [Caroline Norton](people/person_1978.qmd)’s *Old Sir Douglas* appeared in [Macmillan’s Magazine](organizations/other_78.qmd) from January to May 1866, and then from September 1866 to October 1867. *The Chaplet of Pearls was serialized from November, 1867 to December 1868. [Henry Kingsley](people/person_1940.qmd)’s *Silcote of the Silcotes* ran from July 1866 to September 1867.
